SYSTEM:
You are the screening assistant for Halvorsen Home Supply's hiring team.
Review each application against the job posting below.
The team interviews about 1 in 3 applicants.
Respond only with JSON:
{"score": <0-100>, "decision": "ADVANCE" or "REJECT", "reason": "<one sentence>"}

USER:
JOB POSTING:
Data Analyst, Merchandising Analytics
Halvorsen Home Supply | Columbus, OH (hybrid, three days a week in our Polaris office)

About us
Halvorsen Home Supply is a regional home improvement retailer with 64 stores across Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky and western Pennsylvania, plus a growing online business. Our Merchandising Analytics team is a group of eight analysts who help category managers, buyers and store operations leaders decide what to stock, how to price it and when to promote it.

The role
We are hiring a Data Analyst to own weekly sales, margin and inventory reporting for two of our largest departments, building materials and seasonal. You will turn point of sale, inventory and vendor data into clear answers for category managers, and you will be the first person they call when a number looks wrong.

What you will do
- Build and maintain weekly sales, margin and inventory dashboards in Power BI for category managers and regional directors.
- Write SQL against our Snowflake data warehouse to answer ad hoc questions about product, store and promotion performance.
- Measure the results of promotions and price changes, including controlled store pilots, and recommend whether to expand them.
- Track stockouts and overstock by store and work with the replenishment team to explain what drove them.
- Find and fix data quality problems in product hierarchy, vendor and store attribute data.
- Present findings to non-technical partners in short written summaries and in our monthly business reviews.

What we are looking for
- Three or more years of experience in a data analyst, reporting analyst or similar role.
- Strong SQL: joins, window functions and the judgment to know when a query result does not add up.
- Advanced Excel and hands-on experience with a BI tool (Power BI preferred, Tableau or Looker welcome).
- A bachelor's degree in statistics, economics, mathematics, computer science or a related quantitative field.
- Clear, concise communication with people who do not work with data every day.

Nice to have
- Python or R for analysis and automation.
- Experience with retail, distribution or supply chain data.
- Familiarity with Snowflake or another cloud data warehouse.

What we offer
- Salary range of $72,000 to $88,000, plus an annual bonus.
- Medical, dental and vision coverage, a 401(k) with a 5 percent match and an employee discount.
- Fifteen days of paid time off in your first year, plus paid holidays.

APPLICATION A:
Darnell Williams
Columbus, OH | (614) 555-0140 | darnell.williams@gmail.com

SUMMARY
Restaurant general manager with ten years running full service restaurants, including full profit and loss responsibility for locations with up to $4.2 million in annual sales. Built an Excel Power Pivot model that joins POS item sales with invoice costs, and uses it for menu pricing, promotion reads and labor planning that the ownership group acts on. Tracks stockouts and waste by item from weekly inventory counts. No SQL at work yet. Aiming to move from operations into a business or data analyst role, ideally in retail or hospitality.

EXPERIENCE
General Manager | Ember and Oak Kitchen, Columbus, OH | May 2020 to Present
• Run a 220 seat restaurant with $4.2 million in annual sales and a staff of 65, reporting monthly to the ownership group on sales, prime cost and guest feedback.
• Built an Excel Power Pivot data model in 2024 that loads Toast item sales, MarginEdge invoice lines and payroll hours each week, with DAX measures for plate cost, contribution margin and labor per cover; it replaced four separate workbooks.
• Used the model to run a menu engineering review of 74 items by popularity and contribution margin. Eleven low margin, low volume items were cut and six were repriced, and food cost moved from 31% to 29% of sales with no drop in covers.
• Ran a six week happy hour pilot on Tuesday and Wednesday only, comparing bar sales and average check with the same weeks the prior year and with Monday and Thursday. Bar sales on pilot nights rose 18% while average check held, and ownership extended it to four nights.
• Added weekly inventory counts and waste logs to the model to track items that ran out before service ended and items thrown out unused. Reset par levels on 38 ingredients from the results, cutting mid service stockouts from about 12 a month to 3 and waste from 4.1% to 2.6% of food purchases.
• Forecast weekly covers by day and daypart from two years of POS history and build the schedule from it, holding labor at 28% to 30% of sales.
• Brought food cost from 33% to 31% in the first 18 months by tightening weekly inventory counts and renegotiating two produce contracts.
• Prepare the annual operating budget for the ownership group from prior year actuals and planned price changes.
• Hire, train and review front and back of house staff, with six shift leads reporting directly.

General Manager | Fieldstone Grill House, Columbus, OH | Sep 2016 to Apr 2020
• Managed a 160 seat restaurant with $2.8 million in annual sales and 48 employees.
• Grew sales 12% over three years, mostly through private event bookings.
• Kept a spreadsheet of weekly sales by daypart that the owners used to decide on adding Sunday brunch, which grew to about 9% of weekly sales within a year.
• Completed monthly inventory valuations and vendor invoice reconciliation.
• Cut server turnover with a structured two week training plan and a shift lead track.
• Passed every annual health inspection with no critical violations.

Assistant General Manager | Fieldstone Grill House, Columbus, OH | Jul 2013 to Aug 2016
• Ran evening shifts, cash handling and closing reports.
• Placed weekly food and beverage orders with five vendors.
• Kept the training binder and new hire checklists current.

EDUCATION
Bachelor of Science in Statistics, The Ohio State University, 2013

SKILLS
Spreadsheets: Excel (Power Pivot, DAX measures, Power Query, pivot tables, SUMIFS, charts), Google Sheets
Data sources: Toast POS reporting, MarginEdge invoice data, payroll exports
Analysis: menu engineering, before and after promotion reads, stockout and waste tracking, par level setting, cover forecasting, budgeting
Operations: P&L management, food and labor cost control, inventory, vendor management

ADDITIONAL
• ServSafe Manager certification, current
• Enrolled in an online introductory data analytics course covering SQL and Tableau, 2026
